title: Who may do what with a file

terminal.description: A shell that starts in the shop's top folder. Read the letters with ls -l before and after each change.

tasks.title: Lock the price list
tasks.description:
Make `prices.csv` in the top folder read-only for everyone: nobody may change it, you included, and everyone may still read it.

Check reads the permissions of `prices.csv` in the top folder: no `w` for anyone, and `r` for the owner, the group and others.
nextSteps: Run `ls -l prices.csv` and read the nine letters after the first one.
Find which of the owner, the group and others have `w` now.
Take `w` away from all of them with `chmod`, and leave `r` alone.
Run `ls -l prices.csv` again and read the letters.
hints: The lesson's part on read-only files says which letter to take away, and from whom.
`chmod` takes who, a sign and a letter. `a` means all three, and `-` takes a letter away.
Run `chmod a-w prices.csv` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Keep the bank details to yourself
tasks.description:
`accounts/bank-details.txt` is for your eyes only. You, its owner, keep `r` and `w`. The group and others get nothing: no `r`, no `w` and no `x`.

Check reads the permissions of `accounts/bank-details.txt`: `r` and `w` for the owner, and nothing for the group or others.
nextSteps: Run `ls -l accounts` and find the owner and the group of `bank-details.txt`.
Read which letters the group and others have now.
Take every letter away from both of them with one `chmod`.
Run `ls -l accounts` again: the owner's letters are the same as before.
hints: Two of the three kinds of people lose everything here, and the owner keeps what they have.
Who can be two letters at once, such as `go`. Take away `rwx`, or set them to nothing with `=`.
Run `chmod go-rwx accounts/bank-details.txt` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Lock the old price lists
tasks.description:
Lock the three price lists in `archive` the way `prices.csv` is locked: nobody may change them, and everyone may still read them. The `archive` folder itself stays open: its owner keeps `w` on it, so next year's list can go in.

Check reads the permissions of each price list in `archive` and of the folder: no `w` on any list, `r` on each for everyone, and `w` still on the folder for its owner.
nextSteps: Run `ls -l` in the top folder to see the folder's own letters, and `ls -l archive` to see the lists.
Write one `chmod` that names every list at once, with a pattern.
Leave the folder's own letters as they are.
List both again and compare the letters.
hints: A folder's letters and the letters of the files in it are separate. This task changes only the files.
A pattern such as `archive/*.csv` hands `chmod` every list at once. Do not name the folder itself.
Run `chmod a-w archive/*.csv` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Change a price and lock the list again
tasks.description:
The fox poster now costs 22.00. In `prices.csv`, change the line `fox poster A3,18.00` to `fox poster A3,22.00`. Keep every other line as it is, in its place. Then lock the list again, as in the first task.

Check compares `prices.csv` with its lines at the start, with only the fox poster's line changed, and reads its permissions: no `w` for anyone.
nextSteps: Try to change the line now, and read what the editor or the terminal says.
Change the fox poster's line and save the file.
Lock the list again, then look at it with `ls -l` and `cat`.
hints: A locked file has to be unlocked before anyone can change it, you included.
`chmod u+w` gives the owner `w` back. After the change, take `w` from everyone again.
Run `chmod u+w prices.csv`, change the line in the editor and let it save, then run `chmod a-w prices.csv`.
